scope: Corollary 5.5 (The primitive map at every polarized fiber) of the manuscript “A Conditional Reduction for Algebraic Kuga–Satake Correspondences” (preprints/A-Conditional-Reduction-for-Algebraic-Kuga-Satake-Correspondences-September-10-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 032 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e59953bdc640de5f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 17. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a polarized moduli component, and assume that at very general points the nonzero algebraic input of Theorem 1.1 holds. Then at every (S0, h) in that component the standard full primitive Clifford tensor is induced by a rational codimension-two algebraic cycle. The same conclusion holds if the hypothesis is made outside countably many proper closed analytic subsets in a full-dimensional polarized period chart about each desired point.
